A1.justification: Both complete 32-page PDFs describe UniPath and include Appendices A–H. Text extraction, rendered-page comparison and embedded-image checks support a reliable comparison; pages 2–32 are identical.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original image-generation evaluations, classification experiments, human judgments and ablations, including Tables 1–2 and S1–S4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including generation, classification, human-evaluation and ablation outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same frozen Patho-R1 backbone, three-stream control architecture, prototype retrieval, DiT generator and flow-matching objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pathology training corpora, refined 68K subset, 10K generation/control test set, PathMMU benchmark and Kather-CRC-2016 classification task. No domain or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within the generation, understanding, judge and downstream experiments. Tables 1–2 and S1–S3 retain the same comparison methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, image processing, evaluation metrics, the 60/20/20 control-task split, few-shot settings and judge procedures are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices D/F.

E4.justification: The data and stream ablations, paraphrase examples, leakage checks, prototype-count sensitivity, retrieval-component ablations and qualitative case studies are identical, including Section 5.7 and Appendices E–G.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds for downstream classification, mean±standard deviation in Table S3, and the same inter-annotator agreement analysis in Appendix F.4. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plots and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains UniPath's Patho-FID of 80.86 and CLIP-Score of 0.348; Tables S1–S4 also match exactly.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), including the semantic-token, retrieval, conditioning and flow-matching definitions, are identical. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about unified understanding/generation, semantic and prototype control, data contributions and performance. Only the abstract's resource-access statement changes.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations remain identical, including the explanation of Show-o2's CLIP-Score advantage, dependence on prototype coverage, resolution limitations and potential data biases in Appendices A–C.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future promise to release datasets, complete source code and pretrained weights with a stated dataset/code access link to the Hanminghao/UniPath repository. The explicit weights-release promise is omitted. Implementation details are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or actual availability.

R1.justification: Section 2, the 51 references and the paper's positioning relative to pathology and unified multimodal models are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract's final sentence is rewritten, the displayed date changes from December 25, 2025 to February 27, 2026, and version information is updated. Author-name capitalization changes only in PDF metadata; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract reflows around the newly displayed repository hyperlink, and the first-page version stamp changes. All scientific figures, tables, captions and page layouts from page 2 onward are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a concrete dataset/code access pointer where v1 only promised future release, modestly improving resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged. The omitted weights-release promise and unverified repository contents limit the gain to access documentation.
